text:
Lena K.: Hey all 1 starting today! A few quick security onboarding q's: 1) Can I use my personal laptop until corp device ships? 2) Is VPN required when working from home? 3) What's the process to get sandbox KMS access for a demo? 4) I saw a "phish sim" email 2 do I need to do anything now?

Mira (People Ops): Welcome Lena :wave: 1) Short answer: personal is allowed temporarily but must be enrolled and disk-encrypted. 2) VPN required for any prod or internal repo access. 3) KMS: request via infra ticket, add manager approval. 4) Phish sim is mandatory for all new hires  typically during week 1 or 2.

IT Helpdesk: @Lena K. - If you use personal laptop, follow the BYOD checklist: https://redwood.infra/byod. Main steps: enable FileVault (macOS) or BitLocker (Windows), install corp MDM agent, and join SSO via Okta. VPN client: use "redwood-vpn" (macOS brew cask: brew install --cask redwood-vpn). To enroll FileVault quickly: ```sudo fdesetup enable -user $(whoami)``` (you'll need admin). Paste fdesetup status output in the ticket.

Lena K.: Thanks  can I use Authy (desktop) for MFA or do I need phone/YubiKey? Also, for demos I need a sandbox key that can decrypt example payloads  will manager approval be enough?

Security Team: Authy OK for TOTP on personal devices but YubiKey required for engineer roles that access prod secrets. Sandbox KMS role is "kms:DevSandboxDecrypt" and generally requires your manager + owner of the sandbox to sign off. We also need you to acknowledge the Data Handling addendum (link below). DM us if the demo touches customer PII. https://redwood.internal/security/data-handling

IT Helpdesk: If you want to avoid using personal phone, you can request a temporary hardware token shipped to you  open the ticket and choose "MFA token". For attaching proof of encryption: on mac run ```fdesetup status``` and include output; on win run ```manage-bde -status C:``` and paste.

Lena K.: Re: VPN  if I'm on a trusted home network, can I skip VPN for low-risk tasks (docs, slack)?

Security Team: No; policy is VPN for internal resources to ensure routing & logging. You can access public docs/slack without VPN but anything behind Okta SSO or internal IP ranges requires it. If latency is an issue, request a split-tunnel exception via the ticket and include justification.

Mira (People Ops): I'll kick off the ticket for device enrollment and MFA token request and tag your manager. Also the LMS security course shows up as "Security Basics for Employees" and has a short quiz due EOW.

Onboard Bot: Reminder created  Security Basics quiz due in 5 days. Phishing sim window for new hires: 1764990000 - 1765076400.

Lena K.: Awesome, thanks everyone. One last thing  is there a process for temporary access sharing (pairing session) without creating permanent shared creds?

Security Team: Use ephemeral session tokens via the internal "just-in-time" access flow: https://redwood.internal/just-in-time. Never share long-lived credentials or post secrets in Slack. If you need screen-sharing for demos, prefer Zoom with recording off and get a NDA if demoing customer data.

Lena K.: Got it. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
